solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I don't know colonist walking to the right

parts.note: saying 'pass' is the quiz contestant's way of admitting ignorance
an ant lives in a colony, so it is a colonist

explanation.surface: A settler who cannot answer a question while strolling off rightwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The term is heraldic: a beast drawn walking with one forepaw raised, facing dexter, the viewer's left but the shield's right.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic term for an animal shown in a walking pose, heading toward the dexter side of the shield.

clue.text: Pop instrument

definitions.meaning: to pop something is slang for leaving it with a pawnbroker
a person used as a tool by others, like a chess piece of least value

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: hocking goods, and a person manipulated as someone else's tool.

clue.text: Small person on budget holiday finds beetle

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
someone holidaying cheaply in a tent or van is a camper

explanation.surface: A short holidaymaker on a shoestring trip comes across an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the insect noun; it is the verb meaning to hurry about.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle off is to scurry or dash away quickly, a synonym for running playfully.

clue.text: Central section of program is seldom at fault

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the middle of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A software fault rarely shows up in the core part of the code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or out of order is said to be at fault; both describe an error.

clue.text: Came to power and filched deliveries

parts.note: to filch is to steal, to take
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: Someone seized office and also pinched the parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is the set of six balls a cricket bowler delivers in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming control of a government or company is an idiom for gaining command.

clue.text: Thoroughly cack-handed husband getting around DIY at first

indicators.note: the clumsy word plus its partner wrap themselves about the next piece

parts.note: clumsy, lacking skill

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A clumsy spouse botching home improvements, done properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting around' puts INEPT plus H around D, the first letter of DIY (do-it-yourself), splitting the result as IN-D-EPTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating a topic comprehensively, with detailed coverage, is to study it with thoroughness.

clue.text: Mountain dwellers — one cross, bitten by insects

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the cross is held in the mouths of the insects, so it sits inside them

parts.note: bees are insects
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An angry animal in the hills has been stung by bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one cross' reads as an annoyed animal; one is I and cross is X.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild goats of the Alps and other high ranges, which live among crags and peaks.

clue.text: Chastening language used in four consecutive letters

indicators.note: the language is placed inside the four-letter run

parts.note: a run of four letters in alphabetical order, here D, E, F, G
Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Humbling speech made with only a few letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastening someone takes them down a peg, reducing their pride or confidence.

clue.text: Turned up about a job relating to apostle

indicators.note: the turned word sits around the single letter that follows
turning the little word over in a down clue reads it backwards

parts.note: a line of work is a job

explanation.surface: Someone appeared regarding a post connected with a disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses UP to PU; 'about' puts it around A for PAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective describing the writings or teachings of St Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles.

clue.text: Like do-gooder, say, loathed admitting thirst outside pub

indicators.note: letting in, so the other letters go inside this word

parts.note: hated means loathed

indicators.note: the craving word goes round the pub abbreviation

parts.note: a yen is a craving or thirst
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A busybody, detested for wanting a drink near the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do-gooder' is an example of a word joined by a dash, hence the 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word do-gooder is written with a dash joining its parts, an example of such compounds.

clue.text: Vexatious bridge pair happen to claim honour

parts.note: in bridge the partnerships are North-South and East-West, so W and E are a pair

indicators.note: the event word takes hold of the honour, putting it inside

parts.note: to arise is to happen
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Irritating card partners make a fuss to grab a distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, West and East play as partners, so 'bridge pair' can mean WE. 'to claim' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and irksome things are both annoying, so tedious is close to vexatious.

clue.text: Fine beef steak, not much of a dish?

definitions.note: a dish here is an attractive person, so the phrase means a dowdy one

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
rump is a cut of beef steak

explanation.surface: A good cut of beef that disappoints as a plated meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for a good-looking person, not a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowdy, unattractive woman is the opposite of a looker, which slang calls a dish.

clue.text: Various old poets gathering in private ground after theatre visit?

indicators.note: the letters appear in assorted arrangements
ground in the sense of crushed and broken up, so these letters are scrambled too

explanation.surface: Several ancient bards meeting on someone's estate after seeing a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not the playhouse; the poets and private are all mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing care or a period that follows surgery, once the patient leaves the operating room.

clue.text: Socrates did, endlessly shivering out in the cold

indicators.note: shaking about, so the letters are jumbled
the last letter of the short word is dropped

explanation.surface: The Greek philosopher trembled without end in the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: Socrates plus DI (did without its end) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excluded or shunned by a group is figuratively left out in the cold.

clue.text: Affected kid in old Japanese capital

indicators.note: the trick goes inside the coin

parts.note: the sen was a former Japanese coin, so money or capital
to kid is to fool, to trick

explanation.surface: A child was moved while in Japan's former seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city such as Kyoto, but it means money: the sen coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck down or badly hit by illness or grief is to be afflicted by it.

clue.text: Flirtatious lady snaffles last of ginger cake

indicators.note: grabs, taking the letter inside

parts.note: a coquette is a flirt

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A flirt grabs the final bit of a ginger sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fried roll of minced food in breadcrumbs, a fishcake-like savoury patty.

clue.text: European dons measure area: places timber may be sourced from

definitions.text: places timber may be sourced from

indicators.note: puts on, like clothing, so the measure wraps the letter

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A continental academic gauges the space where wood is harvested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university tutors, but it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of pinetum, a plantation of conifers, so a source of softwood.

clue.text: Give up on insignificant Bergman film

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to give is to yield or sag under weight
light means trivial, insignificant

explanation.surface: Abandoning someone unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give up' looks like quit; it is SAG read up the grid. The 1944 film starred Ingrid Bergman.
explanation.definitionFit: Title of the 1944 thriller for which Ingrid Bergman won an Oscar.

clue.text: Backward daughter put her foot down again?

parts.note: retro means looking back, backward

explanation.surface: A slow girl who insisted once more on her way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put her foot down' suggests insisting; read literally it is stepping again.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of retread: walked over the same ground once more, stepping a second time.

clue.text: Editor's gripped by baseless lethargy — it could harm sub

indicators.note: held within, so the editor goes inside
in a down clue the base is the bottom letter, which is removed

parts.note: torpor is sluggishness, lethargy

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor, sluggish without reason, could hurt a subeditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' looks like a subeditor; it is a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is a weapon that can sink a submarine.

clue.text: Material I bought originally in mix-up

indicators.note: the letters go inside the confusion

parts.note: a tangle is a confusion, a mix-up

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Fabric I purchased in a muddle at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth; it is the adjective, real.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concrete and real, able to be touched, is physical or substantial.

clue.text: Monarchy shows shrewdness, getting to grips with technology

indicators.note: grasping, so the other part goes inside

parts.note: brain means intelligence, shrewdness
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A royal house displays acumen in tackling tech.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Kingdom is an example of a constitutional kingdom with a sovereign.

clue.text: Programs needing prize — 500 put up by English

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter is shifted higher up the word

parts.note: an award is a prize
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Software that wants an award costing 500, raised by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' moves the D of AWARD higher in the down entry, giving ADWAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising-supported software, a kind of computer application showing adverts.

clue.text: Culprit's code I cracked forms basis of case

indicators.note: a code is cracked, so its letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Deciphering the offender's cipher gives the prosecution its grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal Latin for the body of facts showing a crime occurred, which a prosecution needs.

clue.text: Intriguing group of Spanish gents? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, a play on the exclamation meaning very much

parts.note: caballeros are Spanish gentlemen

explanation.surface: A plotting band of Spanish gentlemen; and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'very much', but here half the word is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret clique of plotters, a faction scheming in private for power.

clue.text: One copper standing up to catch another fly

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the other piece inside
in a down clue the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant, a police officer
another copper, here the metal, chemical symbol Cu

explanation.surface: A policeman stands to catch a second officer who is dashing away.
explanation.walkthrough: The two coppers differ: a detective sergeant and the metal copper.
explanation.definitionFit: To scud is to race along swiftly, as clouds do before the wind.

clue.text: Had room for second piano in rented property

indicators.note: the piano letter goes inside the property word

parts.note: a let is a property rented out
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A rental house had space for a second piano.
explanation.walkthrough: A holiday cottage that 'sleeps six' has room for six overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Accommodated overnight: a house can be said to sleep a given number of guests.

clue.text: Unusual Gaelic bar shown symbolically

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd Scottish pub depicted through symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics using letters and symbols for quantities, as in equations, is this branch.

clue.text: See retiring CO fade from memory outside Home Counties

indicators.note: the fading word wraps around the reversed officer

parts.note: to die out is to be forgotten

indicators.note: withdrawing, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, the counties around London

explanation.surface: Watch a commanding officer stepping down and being forgotten outside London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's seat, not the verb. The Home Counties are those surrounding London in South-East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under that bishop's authority, a synonym.

clue.text: Clawed back most of information going about by oneself

indicators.note: surrounding, so the reversed letters go around the next piece
the shortened word is read backwards
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: data means information
lone means solitary, by oneself

explanation.surface: Someone fought their way back, mostly informed, while wandering solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last A of DATA; 'back' turns DAT into TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Having talons, the sharp hooked nails of a bird of prey, means having claws.
